newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end higher after hectic session.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end higher after hectic session.

text.p: Singapore shares ended firmer on Thursday after a hectic session in which more than 355 million shares were traded, with electronic shares leading the surge.
Dealers said gains were across the board with Malaysian shares traded over the counter also making strong gains.
"It does not take much to spark a rally as Singapore, and especially Malaysia, has been pretty dead for a while," said one broker with a Singapore firm.
Dealers said several electronic related shares touched new highs, absorbing several rounds of profit taking through the the day.
"All the printed circuit board makers have shot up to new highs, like Elec & Eltech and Wong's Circuits ," said one broker.
Elec & Eltech ended at US$7.20, up 45 cents, and Wong's at US$2.16, up five cents.
The SES electronics index touched a new high of 151.07 before easing to end at 150.60, up 6.35 points or 4.40 percent.

Dealers said several Indonesian linked counters also shot up on speculative trading, with ice cream seller ABR Holdings topping the list. It rose 42 cents or 37 percent to end at S$1.55. Baker Delifrance ended 18 cents higher at S$1.86 after announcing an Indonesian joint venture.
The Straits Times Industrial index ended 6.59 points up at 1,981.28.
Among the losers were City Developments, down 30 cents, and Keppel Corp.
